text: CITY ATTORNEY'S IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE
Measure would amend the East Palo Alto Municipal Code to establish term limits for City Councilmembers.

Currently, the Municipal Code does not limit how long an individual may serve on the City Council. This measure would limit individuals to a maximum of three (3) consecutive four- year terms, or a total of twelve (12) years. A partial term of more than two (2) years would count as a full term.

The limitation would apply only to terms that begin after the ordinance takes effect, which under Elections Code Section 9217, would be in December 2026. Any terms served by an individual on the City Council before that date would not count towards the term limit.
This measure was placed on the ballot by the City Council of the City of East Palo Alto. It requires a majority vote to pass.
Voting "Yes" means adopting these term limits for City Councilmembers.
Voting "No" means City Councilmembers would not be subject to term limits. Evy-I
John D. Lé City Attorney
FILED OFFICE OF THE CHIEF ELECTIONS OFFICER SAN MATEO COUNTY
MARK CHU OFFICER

text: ARGUMENT IN FAVOR OF MEASURE Vote YES on Measure Today, there is no limit on how long councilmembers can serve on the City Council . Someone can serve for decades. This measure limits Council members to three consecutive four-year terms, twelve years of service, after which they must step away for two years before seeking a seat again. It is not a ban. It is a pause that reopens every seat to the community. Term limits bring new voices, new ideas, and new energy into City Hall. They widen the path for residents who have never seen a realistic opening to run. They ensure that experience is renewed rather than merely accumulated, and that our government reflects the East Palo Alto of today, Measure is written to be fair. It applies going forward only. No current Council member's past service is counted against them, and no one is removed from a seat they hold today. Six Cities across San Mateo County already have term limits. The San Mateo County Board of Supervisors is limited to three terms and twelve years, exactly what this measure asks of us, The legislators who represent us in Sacramento, the Governor, and the President are all term-limited. Twelve years is a full and generous opportunity to serve. After that, our neighbors deserve a real chance to choose someone new, and the best ideas should have to earn support all over again. A vote for Measure is a vote for accountability, for competition, and for a City Council that stays close to the people it serves. Please join us. Vote YES on Measure

text: Ballot Argument Against Term Limits—Measure
East Palo Alto already has term limits. It's called voting out your city representatives when they are not meeting the community's needs. Vote No on Measure

We already have that opportunity every two years in November. EPA voters have on numerous occasions not reelected councilmembers, selecting other candidates instead. Don't be fooled into voting for a law limiting the people's choice. Vote No on Measure

San Mateo County has 20 cities. There's a sound reason why only 6 cities have term limits and 14 cities, a supermajority, do not. East Palo Altans disadvantage ourselves with term limits, handicapping our seasoned elected representatives from holding leadership positions on vital regional bodies. It takes time to be known and supported countywide by electeds. This measure gets in the way of that. Vote No on Measure
EPA is a small city that punches above its weight precisely because our representatives are more likely able to hold regional positions. Let's keep it that way

If you don't like an elected official, just vote them out of office. Don't limit the people's ability to vote for someone with proven and effective experience and who they trust is doing a good job. That is what this measure will do if passed. It hurts EPA. Vote No on Measure End
Is/ Javanni Brown; Ravneel Chaudhary; Luis Rosas 21b

text: Don't be fooled. Vote No on Measure CC.
The sole signer of the Argument in Favor asks East Palo Alto voters to restrict our choices at the ballot box. Experience counts and he wants to cancel it.

Council seats don't need to be "reopened." They're already open every election to any citizen who desires to run. Challengers can run, incumbents can lose, and voters will choose new leadership whenever they believe change is needed. This measure removes a choice from voters. Vote No on Measure CC.

The argument claims term limits will bring new voices, competition, and accountability. It guarantees none of these. Term limits do not create candidates, increase voter participation, or guarantee better representation. Vote No on Measure CC.

Comparisons to county, state, and federal offices ignore East Palo Alto's circumstances. It also ignores that 70% of cities in the County have no term limits. Our five-member city council represents East Palo Alto on important regional bodies, where experience and relationships, built up over years, can strengthen our city's voice. Let's not jeopardize that. Vote No on Measure CC.

Accountability comes from elections, not from ill-informed ballot measures like this one. If a councilmember is not serving our community well, vote them out. If voters believe someone is effectively representing East Palo Alto, they should retain the right to reelect them. Vote No on Measure CC.
Don't voluntarily surrender your voting power. Trust yourself and East Palo Alto voters to decide who represents us.
Vote No on Measure CC.
Is/ Javanni Brown; Ravneel Chaudhary; Luis Rosas
FLED
SAN MATEO COUNTY
